title: Cut total batch size 4x (2^19 -> 2^17)
description: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**17 and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 -> 64 (grad_accum 2 -> 1); nothing else changed.
reflection: Exact wash: val_bpb 0.997358 vs baseline 0.997359. My premise was wrong -- throughput is ~1.65M tok/s, so the baseline already got ~950 optimizer steps (not ~300) in the 5 minutes. At 2^17 we got 3148 steps on 412.6M tokens vs the baseline's ~480M: 3.3x more steps bought exactly enough per-token efficiency to pay for 14% fewer tokens, and no more. So the batch-size axis is flat here -- neither 2^18 nor 2^16 is likely to move val_bpb. Two things for later rounds: (1) steady-state MFU dropped 39.8% -> 33.1% because per-step optimizer/Python overhead is amortised over 4x less data, so smaller batches actively cost tokens; (2) LRs were left unchanged while the batch shrank 4x, i.e. the effective per-token LR rose 4x with zero instability, which says the current LRs sit on the conservative side of the stability edge and raising MATRIX_LR/EMBEDDING_LR at the 2^19 batch is untested and cheap. Future runs should target model scale (depth/width) and LR, not batch size.
